articles.title: Sentence embeddings in JAX, after Transformers v5 dropped it
articles.excerpt: Hugging Face Transformers v5 removed its TensorFlow and JAX code to focus on PyTorch. If you used FlaxBertModel or FlaxAutoModel to compute sentence embeddings in JAX, those classes are gone. This pos…
articles.body: Hugging Face Transformers v5 removed its TensorFlow and JAX code to focus on PyTorch. If you used FlaxBertModel or FlaxAutoModel to compute sentence embeddings in JAX, those classes are gone. This post shows how to compute sentence embeddings in JAX with eqx-zoo , an open-source library that loads Hugging Face checkpoints as plain Equinox modules. The embeddings match sentence-transformers to within float32 rounding, and the post ends with how that's verified. We'll cover English and multilingual models, a small semantic search, and Qwen3-Embedding , a modern embedding model built on a language model. Install pip install eqx-zoo tokenizers eqx-zoo brings in JAX and Equinox ; tokenizers is Hugging Face's fast tokenizer library, which we'll use to turn text into token ids.

articles.title: MCP connection errors explained: 404 on /sse, 406 Not Acceptable, session 400s, 402
articles.excerpt: MCP Streamable HTTP is one URL. The client POSTs JSON-RPC to it and may open a GET stream on the same URL; nothing else is part of the address. Most connection failures we see in our own server log ar…
articles.body: MCP Streamable HTTP is one URL. The client POSTs JSON-RPC to it and may open a GET stream on the same URL; nothing else is part of the address. Most connection failures we see in our own server log are a client talking to a different address than the one it was given, or sending the wrong headers. Here is what each status means and the fix, with the exact messages the official TypeScript and Python SDKs send. 404 Not Found on /sse , or with /mcp appended The earlier HTTP+SSE transport (protocol revision 2024-11-05) opened a GET to an SSE URL and read an endpoint event that named a second URL for POSTs. Streamable HTTP (2025-03-26 and later) replaced both with a single URL.

articles.title: 9 Legend of Zelda Side Quests Scarier than Any Horror Game
articles.excerpt: Cursed spider families, a ship that sails only at night, and a mummified father in a closet: nine Zelda side quests that belong in a horror story
articles.body: The Legend of Zelda has never been particularly shy about depicting curses, ghosts, and the walking dead (or ReDead). Its optional side quests are where Nintendo tends to let all three run wild. The series has always worked this way — usually giving you a bright, whimsical surface to explore with something rotten and/or horrifying tucked away, should you decide to look under that friendly surface. In the main story, that dread hides inside dungeons and boss fights. In the side quests, the dread has moved into the house next door, where it’s a bit more startling to discover. Curious what nightmares are hiding for Link throughout his various adventures? Check all the closets in the basement, first. Then read on, if you dare.

articles.title: Why Your AI Cost Dashboard Never Matches Your Invoice
articles.excerpt: If you've ever looked at a token counter after a long session with Claude Code, Codex, or Copilot and tried to reconcile it with your actual bill, you've probably hit a wall. Here's why that number is…
articles.body: If you've ever looked at a token counter after a long session with Claude Code, Codex, or Copilot and tried to reconcile it with your actual bill, you've probably hit a wall. Here's why that number is structurally unreliable, not just imprecise. 1. Most dashboards show list-price tokens, not what you paid. Anthropic's own docs are explicit about it: spend figures in the Claude Code console "are estimates for analytics purposes" ( https://code.claude.com/docs/en/analytics?utm_source=devto&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=cost-estimate ). If you're on a flat-rate plan like Max or Copilot Business, there's no per-request price at all — you're paying for a quota, and the tool still shows you an API-equivalent cost that has nothing to do with your invoice. 2.

articles.title: Margaret Hamilton, Apollo Programmer, Dies at 90: Legacy in Space Exploration Endures
articles.excerpt: Analytical Reconstruction of Margaret Hamilton's Legacy Announcement System The announcement of Margaret Hamilton's passing triggers a multifaceted system designed to honor her legacy, preserve her co…
articles.body: Analytical Reconstruction of Margaret Hamilton's Legacy Announcement System The announcement of Margaret Hamilton's passing triggers a multifaceted system designed to honor her legacy, preserve her contributions, and ensure her impact endures. This system, comprising five interrelated mechanisms, underscores the complexity of commemorating a figure whose work revolutionized software engineering and space exploration. By examining these mechanisms, we reveal the delicate balance between public recognition, historical accuracy, and personal respect—all critical to maintaining Hamilton's legacy as a trailblazer for women in STEM and a cornerstone of modern technology. Mechanism 1: Announcement of Death Through Obituary Publication Impact: Initiation of closure and historical documentation.

The programs reflect NASA’s commitment to pioneering research and transformative technologies and advancing the Trump Administration’s vision as outlined in the July report to the President, Science: A New Golden Age. One focuses on peer review and the other on fellowship researchers. “NASA has a proud history of pursuing bold ideas and achieving the near impossible,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman.
